1.title: Cloud Security Fundamentals
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Cloud Security Fundamentals. It covers the exam area five. Trust and security with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point one Describe fundamental cloud security concepts: cybersecurity threats and business implications. Cloud security versus on-premises security. Control, compliance, confidentiality, integrity and availability. Key security terms. Encryption in use, in transit and at rest. Authentication, authorization and auditing. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Trust and security with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Threats and their business impact
1.text: Threats and their business impact. The figure shows this: Common cybersecurity threats and the business harm they cause.

1.title: Threats and their business impact, continued
1.text: Threats and their business impact. D dos (distributed denial of service). What it is: Flood of traffic that overwhelms a service. Business impact: Outage, lost sales. Ransomware. What it is: Malware that encrypts data and demands payment. Business impact: Downtime, ransom, data loss. Cryptomining. What it is: Stolen computing power used to mine cryptocurrency. Business impact: Surprise cloud bills, slow systems. Malware and viruses. What it is: Harmful software. Business impact: Data theft, damage. Phishing. What it is: Fake messages that steal credentials. Business impact: Account takeover, breaches.

1.title: Threats and their business impact, continued
1.text: Threats and their business impact. Misconfiguration. What it is: Wrong settings, such as a public storage bucket. Business impact: Data exposure. Unsecured third-party systems. What it is: Weak partners or suppliers. Business impact: Supply chain breaches. Physical damage. What it is: Fire, flood, theft. Business impact: Hardware and data loss. L L M attacks. What it is: Attacks on A I models, such as prompt injection and data leakage. Business impact: Wrong answers, leaked data. Exam tip: Misconfiguration is one of the most common causes of cloud breaches. It is a customer responsibility.

1.title: Cloud security versus on-premises security
1.text: Cloud security versus on-premises security. You secure everything, including buildings and hardware. Shared responsibility: the provider secures the infrastructure, you secure your data, identities and settings. Security tools bought and maintained by you. Built-in, always-updated security at scale. Slow to patch. Provider patches the platform.

1.title: Core security ideas
1.text: Core security ideas. Control. You decide who accesses your data and where it lives. Compliance. Meeting laws and standards. Confidentiality. Only authorized people can read data. Integrity. Data stays accurate and unaltered. Availability. Systems are there when needed.

1.title: Core security ideas, continued
1.text: Core security ideas. Data loss prevention (D L P). Find and protect sensitive data from leaking. Privileged access. Powerful accounts that need extra protection. Least privilege. Only the access needed for the job. Zero-trust architecture. Never trust, always verify, whatever the network location. Security by default. Systems are safe out of the box. Security posture. The overall state of security: settings, controls, risks. Cyber resilience. Ability to withstand and recover from attacks. Firewall. Allows or blocks traffic by rules. Encryption and decryption. Scramble data with a key; unscramble it with a key.

1.title: Encryption states and the three As
1.text: Encryption states and the three As. At rest. Meaning: Stored on disks and in databases. Protection: Encrypt storage. In transit. Meaning: Moving across networks. Protection: Encrypt connections (T L S). In use. Meaning: Being processed in memory. Protection: Confidential Computing (Module eleven). Authentication. Question: Who are you? Example: Password plus two-step verification or multi-factor authentication. Authorization. Question: What may you do? Example: Identity and Access Management (I A M) roles. Auditing. Question: What did you do? Example: Logs of actions.

1.title: Security operations (SecOps) terms
1.text: Security operations (sec ops) terms. Security posture. The current security state of the environment. Threat intelligence. Knowledge about attackers, their methods and indicators. Threat response. Detecting, investigating and fixing an attack. Exam tip: Authentication equals who, authorization equals what, auditing equals what happened. Two-step verification and M F A strengthen authentication; I A M handles authorization. Exam tip: Match the threat to its symptom: outage from traffic equals D dos, locked files and a ransom note equals ransomware, huge unexpected compute bill equals cryptomining, exposed bucket equals misconfiguration.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company's storage bucket is public by mistake and customer data is exposed. Which threat is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Misconfiguration, a wrong setting. A wrongly configured storage setting is a misconfiguration.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Attackers send a flood of traffic that makes the web shop unavailable. Which threat is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: D dos, which overwhelms a service. A flood of traffic that takes a service offline is a distributed denial-of-service attack.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A user logs in with a password and a code from a phone app. Which security idea is strengthened? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Authentication, which proves who the user is. Two-step verification strengthens authentication.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which control decides which actions a signed-in user may perform on a resource? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Identity and Access Management roles. I A M roles handle authorization, which decides what a user may do.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Customer data is encrypted on its disk and also while it travels between services. Which two states are covered? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: At rest and in transit. Encrypting stored data protects data at rest; encrypting connections protects data in transit.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which statement describes zero-trust architecture? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Never trust, always verify, whatever the location. Zero trust verifies every request and does not trust any location by default.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does ransomware do? Answer: Encrypts data and demands payment. Question two. What is least privilege? Answer: Only the access needed for the job. Question three. What are the three data states for encryption? Answer: At rest, in transit, in use.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does authentication answer? Answer: Who are you? Question five. What is security posture? Answer: The overall state of security. Question six. What is threat intelligence? Answer: Knowledge about attackers and their methods.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Threats: D dos, ransomware, cryptomining, malware, phishing, misconfiguration, third parties, L L M attacks. Cloud versus on-premises: shared responsibility; built-in security; provider patches the platform. Ideas: control, compliance, C I A; least privilege, zero trust, posture, resilience. Encryption: at rest, in transit, in use. Three As: authentication (two-step verification, M F A), authorization (I A M), auditing (logs).
